title: What start(), join() and sleep() guarantee

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Per this page, once `t.join()` has returned, which of thread `t`'s plain (non-volatile) writes is the joining thread sure to see?

options.text: Only its volatile writes, since plain ones may stay in a CPU cache
options.says: The page says all actions of the joined thread are visible after join() returns, with no volatile needed.

options.text: All of its writes, since the JMM orders them before that return
options.says: The page says join() establishes happens-before: all actions in thread B are visible to A after A.join(B) returns.

options.text: None of its writes, since only a shared lock orders two threads
options.says: The page says start() and join() transfer data safely between threads without additional synchronization.

questions.stem: Per this page, what does a thread give up while it is inside `Thread.sleep(millis)`?

options.text: The CPU it was running on, and every monitor it holds
options.says: The page says sleep releases the CPU but not any held monitors.

options.text: Every monitor it holds, but not the CPU it was running on
options.says: The page says sleep releases the CPU, and keeps the monitors.

options.text: The CPU it was running on, but none of the monitors it holds
options.says: The page says Thread.sleep pauses the current thread, releasing the CPU but not any held monitors.

concepts: Thread.sleep() pauses the current thread and gives up the CPU but keeps every monitor it holds.
join() makes every write of the joined thread visible to the joiner, as start() does for the parent's earlier writes, with no volatile or locks.
